item.title: 2.78 Trillion Parameters, 29GB RAM, Half a Token Per Second: Kimi K3 Actually Runs on a Laptop
item.description: WASTE, a pure-C inference engine, squeezes the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 into a 64GB laptop: a 982GB container streams expert weights from disk on demand, measured at 0.5 tok/s. Half a token per second is absurdly slow — but it proves running trillion-scale models locally is an engineering problem, not a money problem.

item.title: Seven Questions About Kimi K3: China's Quiet Fable 5 Contender
item.description: Moonshot AI teased K3 with a 36-second video, but the real story was already unfolding on Chatbot Arena — where an anonymous model codenamed Kivine has been building 3D pages, cloning video effects, and going toe-to-toe with Claude Fable 5. Here's what actually matters.

item.title: Cramming a 400B Model into 48GB: The Magic Behind LLM in a Flash
item.description: An Apple paper from 2023 made it possible to run a 400 billion parameter model on an ordinary MacBook. The core technologies—MoE and quantization—hide an engineering philosophy built around on-demand loading.

item.title: Bring Kimi K2 Thinking Home with 247GB RAM: Dynamic 1-bit GGUF Field Notes
item.description: Step-by-step guide to running Unsloth's Dynamic 1-bit GGUF build of the 1T-parameter Kimi K2 Thinking model on high-end PCs, covering install, download, inference, serving, and troubleshooting.
